Prince of Hell. By night in the Overworld: Azazel's blood, a choir shard and two demon bloods. You no longer hunger nor sleep; you can seize what you look at and hurl it, or ride a mob for twenty seconds. Your eyes turn yellow, and a ring of hellfire bursts out of you at will.

Knight of Hell. Only a Prince who already bears the Mark of Cain (taken from Cain himself) may rise: the Angel Tablet and two demon bloods, with the First Blade to raise it. The Blade answers its Knight and every kill heals you, but the Mark thirsts: go too long without a kill and its bloodlust drinks your Corruption, then your blood (read the page on the Mark). A wave of flame rolls out ahead of you, and you can step out of the shadow behind a foe, whose next wound cuts deeper.

King of Hell. Usurp the throne on the dais of Lucifer's Cage with a Fallen Star and Michael's Grace. Demons and hellhounds obey you, and from the throne every mob near you kneels. You wear the crown and the cloak. The Maw of Hell opens where you look and drags in all near it, and you can descend to Hell with the friends who kneel beside you. Hell is your realm: the same way takes you all back up to where you sleep.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.devils_t: A devil's trap is painted, not built. A square of chalk with a lit candle at each corner, demon blood, salt, paper and red dye on the altar: two traps. Use one on the floor and it paints the whole 3x3 seal around where you clicked, or nothing at all if it does not fit.

Any demon standing on any part of it is held fast. It can still turn and swing at you, but it cannot walk, jump or smoke out of its vessel. That last part is the point: a demon you trap is a demon you get to finish, and its blood with it.
The big ones laugh at paint. Azazel walks right over a trap and burns it on the way.
A great rite can put out the sun. A great circle in the Overworld, by day: two crying obsidian, two black dye, an eye of ender, two demon blood and a sculk catalyst. It costs more mana than a hunter is born with.
For ten minutes the whole world goes dark. Demons walk by day, and more of them. The dead do not burn in the light that is left. Holy strikes bite a little deeper.
Only under an eclipse can the Darkness be called. That is the real reason you would ever do this.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.exorcism: Trap them first. Then a blood circle, two salt and a holy water on the altar, and fire. Every trapped demon within six blocks is cast out of its vessel and sent back down, and each one leaves a hellfire ember behind.

Embers are what the serious rites are paid in: the angel blade, the Hellforge, the Key itself. Every demon you kill in a trap instead of casting out is one ember you will not have. The Exorcise sigil does the same work, one trapped demon at a time.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.familiar: A cat that sits too still, a raven that never flies far: a witch's eyes. A familiar that sees you within sixteen blocks marks you. You glow for three seconds, you feel watched, and every witch nearby turns on you, even the ones who cannot see you.

It steals, too. When it can, about once a minute, it runs at the nearest hunter, snips a lock of hair and bolts back to its witch, who curses you with it from afar until it is taken back. Kill the familiar and the lock drops where it dies.
While it lives within thirty-two blocks of her, its witch's magic is a quarter stronger. A familiar whose witch is dead goes wild after half a minute. Kill it first.

Rowena's working. Name a cat or a parrot you have tamed, with a taglock of its fur or feathers, within sixty-four blocks of the bowl: it becomes your familiar, healed and steadied a while (Regeneration and Resistance for a minute).
A familiar answers to Trace the Familiar. What else it can do for a witch is still being written.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.family_b: Saving people, hunting things. If you are reading this, you already know the world is not what they told you. Demons walk at night wearing people. The dead do not always stay down. And somewhere under it all, something is waiting in a Cage.
This journal is everything I know. Pages fill in as you see things, kill things and get your hands on things: a page you have not earned stays blank. Read in order if you are new. Start with salt.
Chalk comes from calcite and bone meal, and you will draw every circle in this book with it. Mix four chalk with a demon's blood and you have blood chalk, for the circles that matter.
The first tools of the trade
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.0: A frail old man in a wheelchair, and he is always hungry. Call him with rotten flesh, bread, wheat and salt, lit with flint and steel, once Lucifer has fallen. His ground is dead farmland and rotten crops.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.1: Near him your hunger drains away, and whatever you eat close to him feeds him instead. Then he stands up, and his starving thralls shuffle in to be eaten: if one reaches him he drinks its soul and heals, and he feeds on anything living nearby too. Kill them on the way.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.2: On his black horse he feeds on you: he lifts a hunter and drains health and hunger. Everyone else, hit him hard to make him let go. Alone, hold on: he drops you when there is little left.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.find_the: The page for this spell is never found by chance. It falls at your feet the moment you have beaten every great enemy before him: Azazel, Lilith, Lucifer, the Broken Chorus, Metatron, the Darkness and Lucifer Uncaged.
Cast in the Overworld, the smoke draws a map with his mark on it: the Author's Address. From then on, he waits for you at home.
Fallen Star, ink, paper, holy water
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.fly_swar: Pestilence's flies, a buzzing cloud that chases you, blinds you and leaves you sick. Steel goes straight through them; only fire takes them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.four_hor: To open the Cage itself, down in Hell, the Key is not enough. It wants the rings of the four Horsemen, and there is only one way to get a Horseman's ring: win it from him. Once Lucifer has fallen they will answer a call.
War, Famine and Pestilence come up here in the world, each to his own rite, in any order. Death comes too, but only for a hunter who offers him the other three rings. He gives them back, win or lose.
Each one lays his own ground over the arena and rides his horse for the last part of the fight. Beat him and he leaves his ring, his likeness and his horse, every time you beat him.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.four_sch: Every effect sigil, every bowl spell and every rite belongs to one of four schools. The school is the colour its light burns in, the mastery it trains and the discount it earns. A spell takes the school of its first effect; forms and modifiers belong to none, and are drawn in plain chalk white.
Enochian is Heaven's tongue, gold with a white heart: Smite, Mend, Banishing, and the Ward, the one form that is Heaven's own. Holy water and consecrations are Enochian rites.
Infernal is Hell's craft, red fire with orange embers: Hellfire, and the summonings and pacts that call on the pit.
Witchcraft is the old art, magenta smoke on plum: Frost among the sigils, and most of what the spell bowl does, from hex bags to locating spells.
Hunter is the plain lore of salt, silver and iron, steel grey with a blue edge: Repel, Reveal, Exorcise and the Snare, and the rites that drive things out.
Infernal: fire red and ember orange
A pagan god of mischief, they say, who plays deadly pranks on the people who deserve them. He is not. He is Gabriel, the archangel who ran away from his brothers' war and hid in plain sight. Bait him by night with sweets inside a ring of holy oil, and he drags you into TV Land.

Lay two holy oils, a cake and two sugar in a small circle in the Overworld, by night, and wake it with the Trickster's Bait; the bait is eaten every time. He steps out of the fire laughing, and the world round the altar turns into a television studio. Nobody else's road needs him: he is a side show, for the fun of it.

He fights through four channels, a quarter of his strength each, and changes channel when you take it: static, a new set built round you, a new costume. In the sitcom, the game show and the hospital he plays by the show's rules, and so must you. In the commercial, five of him stand at five podiums, and only one is real.

He is not a fair fighter, but he plays fair by his own rules: learn each channel's and he is not as strong as he looks. (TV Land, in this book, tells them channel by channel.) Win, and he leaves his toys.
He can be baited again, as often as you like, one bait each time: then he leaves his trophy and some candy, and now and then his remote or his blade.
What he leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.gabriel_: An archangel blade with a golden edge, and his sense of humour: now and then a strike calls up two fleeting doubles of you, who strike the same foe a little more before they wink out.

Gabriel's oldest trick: more of himself. His doubles wear what he wears and grin the way he grins, but one blow and they are gone. In the sitcom they come through the doors as extras; in the hospital they are nurses in white caps, walking to him to patch him up; in the commercial they are the spokesmen at the podiums. A Reveal sigil dissolves one on the spot.
One of him. Or is it?
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.garrison: Soldiers of Heaven loyal to Raphael, in storm grey and silver, their wings folded. When he is hurt he calls four of them, and each one holds a thread of grace to him while it lives: a ribbon of warm light, and every thread heals him a little every second.

A thread breaks while someone stands in it, and for good when its angel dies. They are only soldiers: a few good blows bring one down. Watch for him laying his hands on a fallen one: he raises one of them, once.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.general_: Michael's own armour, white and gold and written over in Enochian. He leaves one piece each time he falls, one you do not have yet. Worn whole, it wards off holy harm and raises a wing of light that takes a blow for you every thirty seconds.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.0: Old graves hold more than bones. At night a ghost rises near them and haunts whoever comes close: the cold bites and slows you, the lights die, things fly. You will see it only in flickers, and when it lashes out.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.1: Ordinary harm goes straight through it. Cold iron, holy water or anything holy scatters it for a while, and now and then it leaves ectoplasm behind. Salt is a line it cannot cross, walls or no walls. Second Sight and the Reveal sigil show it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.2: It cannot be killed. It stays near its bones and sinks back into its grave at dawn. To be rid of it, see to the bones.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.0: An angel's powers burn Grace, and it comes back on its own: an empty vessel is full again in five minutes, whatever your rank. Standing on consecrated ground doubles that. Pray (crouch and keep still) and it comes three times as fast anywhere; pray on consecrated ground and you are full in half a minute. Consecrated ground is the ground around a ritual altar, a choir altar or an Enochian pillar, or any ground the consecration rite has blessed.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.1: Slaying demons gives Grace too (about a twelfth of your vessel each; a demon boss half of it). In the Darkness's eclipse nothing comes back, and she drinks what you have.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.2: What hurts an angel: holy oil set alight (it cannot cross the ring), the Enochian banishing sigil, an angel blade or Ruby's knife in another's hand (three times the harm), and the Darkness, who drinks Grace in her eclipse. Ghosts will not touch you, and the Host of Heaven does not see you as an enemy.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grand_wi: Only for the one who gave Rowena the Book: the Coven's rite calls her, wherever it is done, and she steps out of the smoke a few blocks from the altar with three sisters round her. Three phases, a third of her strength each.

The Coven's Shield: three coven witches channel into her from seven blocks away, and while even one still channels, every blow on her is swallowed. Break a channeler's own bubble (blows, a salt round, Break Hex) and she stops for twelve seconds; kill her and she is gone for good. Then the shield falls.
The Matriarch's Hexes: a blue circle under every hunter and then frost; an inferno, a red circle six blocks round her; and a violet circle that crushes and pins whoever is still in it.

The Mass Taglock: she holds a lock of everyone's hair. A red circle follows each hunter for two seconds, stops, and then the curse lands, twenty and frailty, on everyone not standing in one of the two green circles Rowena draws. Rowena arrives for this part: she cannot be hurt, and she throws bolts at the coven. Yellow smoke where the Grand Witch is about to land.
The Grand Witch of the Grand Coven
What she leaves: the Coven Staff and her bust the first time (a bust in a rematch)

Rowena's death pleased the Grand Coven. When she falls to someone who kept the Book, the Grand Witch walks out of the smoke on the battlefield. She cannot be harmed, and to anyone else she has nothing to say.
To you she owes one thing: the Mark taken off. She reads the cure from the Book, so you must carry it (she does not keep it), and she wants a vial of your own bound blood.
She leaves after two minutes with nobody near. Read the Book in Rowena's house again and she comes back.
The Grand Witch, owing a debt
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.great_fi: The great ones do not wander. You call them, by rite or by song, and they come with their own ground: a dome closes over the place and there is no leaving it until one of you is done. Only one such fight can hold a world at a time.

Every attack they have is written on the ground before it lands. Learn the colours: red is fire, blue is frost, violet is the mind's reach, gold is judgement, green is the one safe place. Move when you see them, and hit hardest while they recover.
Their ground breaks under them, and puts itself back together once it is over. If everyone falls or runs, they simply leave. Everyone who fought shares the credit for a kill.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grimoire: A book, a vial of Enochian ink, chalk and leather. Ink is an ink sac, sulfur and salt in a glass bottle; you will want plenty of it.
The first time you open it its first pages make sense: Touch, Bolt, Smite and Mend. Everything else you learn from torn sigil pages.

It holds six pages, each a spell. Use it to cast the open page; sneak and turn the scroll wheel (or press the page key) to turn pages. Sneak-use opens this book, and the Scriptorium inside it is where spells are written: each page you inscribe costs a vial of ink.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.0: Heaven is not one place. Every soul that makes it up there gets a Heaven of its own: an island of its best days, in a light that never sets. Yours is waiting already. With Metatron fallen, nobody up there is keeping the door.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.1: Open a gate of light by day in a grace circle in the Overworld: a vial of Grace, two choir shards, two holy water, a golden apple and two feathers, woken with an angel blade (it is not used up). A frame of light stands over the altar for five minutes. Whoever crosses it lands in the Heaven of the hunter who opened it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.2: The first time, your island has to be written: give it a moment. You land on its plaza, by a gate of your own that never closes and always takes you back where you came in. From the plaza a lane of shrines leads off (Memory Lane, in this book), and past them stand a white wing behind a golden seal, a house with its door sealed shut, and a door that opens on a road.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.3: Nothing hurts you here. Fall off the edge and you wake on the plaza, whole. Nothing can be broken or built either, not until your home is yours; then your own yard is yours to change.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.4: A General of the Host needs no gate: they ascend to their own island at will, with the friends who kneel beside them, and the same power takes them all back down the way they came.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven_g: Angels in dark suits and sunglasses, with a wire in one ear: Heaven's security. Naomi calls two or three at a time. While two of them stand she takes less from every blow, so cut them down first. They are only soldiers: a few good blows each.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven_h: When Zachariah's file is closed, the seal on the house's door burns away. It is yours: a room for your trophies, a store room whose chests open for you and the hunters you trust, and the hearth. From now on the yard round the house is yours to build on.

Rest by the hearth and you are mended: whole health, a full belly, every harm and every trace of Hell's torment gone, and a minute of regeneration besides. The fire needs ten minutes before it can do it again.
Coming home no longer needs the full rite. A smaller gate of light, opened at any hour once Zachariah has fallen, sets you down at your own front door.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavenly: At the start of every phase, and every thirty seconds, he hands every hunter a Heavenly Form, numbered I to IV. While you hold one that is not filed, your blows against him are worth a quarter.

Four filing cabinets stand in his office, numbered I to IV. Use the form on the cabinet with its number and it is Approved: for ten seconds every blow you land on him counts half as much again. A clerk's Approval Stamp files any form at once.
Let a form run overdue and he notices: a smite comes down on you for it.
The form, and what files it
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavens_: Zachariah's own seal of office. Carry it in your other hand, or as a charm: the first blow a great enemy lands on you in any minute is halved.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavy_we: The soul scythe is forged at night in a blood circle. Its swings reap a wide arc and drink some of the life they take. Hold use and let go for a crescent of souls.
The hellfire greatsword is slow and heavy. Hold use and let go to cleave a cone in front of you and leave a trail of hellfire behind it.
Both are tier III. The scythe also lights the rite that forges the Ring of Death.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hedge_wi: Not every witch is a crone over a cauldron. These ones walk the forests, swamps, taiga and plains at night, alone or in twos, and they work the same craft you do: sigils and the bowl. They keep six to fourteen blocks off and throw sigil bolts, mostly hexes that jinx you, now and then frost, and once in a while pain.

Get close and she will slip a curse bag into your pack; a protection bag on you turns it away. Hurt her badly and she drinks something foul and mends. Strike her up close and she may vanish in yellow smoke and come out of it eight to fourteen blocks away. Hurt one and every sister within sixteen blocks comes for you.

Left alone near a village, a hedge witch hexes villagers into her thralls, three at most in one place. And if her familiar steals a lock of your hair, she curses you with misfortune every thirty seconds, from wherever she is. A Ward of the Name or a protection bag turns the curse back on her; a Mirror Hex sends it home.
A witch killed by a hunter sometimes leaves a vial of her own blood: something of hers for the bowl.
A hedge witch, satchel full of someone else's hair
What she carries: taglocks, a page, now and then a vial of her blood
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.0: Only those who have beaten Lucifer can open the way. In the Overworld it takes the void circle and the Key, at night, with demon blood, embers, sulfur, a nether star and holy water.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.1: In the Nether it is cheaper: a great circle, two demon blood, two embers, sulfur and a blaze rod, lit with flint and steel at any hour.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.2: A rift stays open twenty minutes. Like the Nether, one step in Hell is eight up here, and the way back opens where you land. Lost down there? A binding circle in Hell with two salt, a holy water and brimstone tears a rift home, to your bed.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.3: A King of Hell needs no rift: they descend at will, with the friends who kneel beside them, and the same power takes them all back up to where they sleep.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell_reg: Hell is a roofed cavern world, like the Nether but taller. The Pit is at its heart; three regions lie around it.

The Ash Wastes burn hottest: brimstone in the rock. The Rack is wet with blood, and chains hang from its roof with meat hooks on the end. Crowley's Corridors are Hell as he ran it, an endless queue: a maze of stone corridors lined with barred cells, some keeping a chest, and in them, contracts.
Shards come from the walls of the Pit, fangs from hellhounds. Demons and occultists roam all of it, and the hounds hunt there in packs.

Hell gets into you. Torment grows while you stay, faster on the Rack, and fades once you leave: red at the edge of sight, whispers, shapes in the fog. It never hurts you. Salt in your off hand or a dash of holy water eases it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hellforg: An anvil, a blast furnace, two hellfire embers and two obsidian in a binding circle raise a Hellforge. It graves runes into weapons, and holds nothing itself.
Put the weapon in, and the runes beside it, as many as it has free slots. Grave costs the weapon's tier times two levels per rune. No more than two alike on one weapon.
Purge strips a weapon for one level and gives the runes back, all but one, lost at random. Think before you grave.

The slot at the far left takes an Ascension Shard. With the shard of the next tier there, Ascend raises the weapon (or a piece of Hunter's Gear, or of the General's armour) one tier, for five levels per tier.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hellhoun: You will not see them. Watch for the air that bends, the smoke of their breath, the paw prints that burn into the ground. They hunt in packs and their bite holds you where you stand.

Holy water, any holy wound or the Reveal sigil shows them for a while; Second Sight outlines them; the Eclipse Sight shows them always. They roam Hell, they come to collect on crossroads debts, and Lilith keeps a few.
Kill one and you may pull a fang. War and Death both want them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.henry_wi: He knocked at dawn, the morning after the Devil fell: a polite young man in a brown suit and a fedora, a briefcase in his hand, who talks like a newsreel. Henry Winchester, a Legacy of the Men of Letters, out of 1958 and somehow standing in front of you.
He offers you a place in the order: a key, a bunker, and every secret the Men of Letters wrote down. Take it and you are an Aspirant; turn him down and he tips his hat and comes back in a few days.
Once you have joined he waits in the bunker's war room, by the lit map table. Talk to him there for a case. What the order knows is kept in the Archive, a tab of this book that only members have.
Henry Winchester, Legacy of the Men of Letters
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hex_bags: Witches' work. A curse bag tucked out of sight curses whoever lingers near it, all but the one who made it: bad luck, softer blows, a hunger that will not quit, and bleeding that gets worse the longer they stay. Now and then it draws worse: lightning, vermin, or after dark, a demon.

Set it down somewhere hidden, tuck it in a chest, or sneak up and slip it into someone's pocket. Found one? Only fire breaks it: flint and steel, a fire charge, any flame that reaches it, or a Purification.

A protection bag in your pack keeps the lesser demons from seeking you out unless you strike first, and no curse bag can touch you. It wears thin while demons are near, and crumbles to dust in the end.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hexed_in: Enochian ink steeped in one school's magic: pour in a potion, add the ink and something to steep it in. A gold nugget steeps it Enochian, blaze powder Infernal, an amethyst shard Witchcraft, salt Hunter. Nothing to steep in, nothing to brew.

Write a page of your grimoire while you carry hexed ink of that spell's school and the Scriptorium uses it instead of plain ink. The page remembers: a spell of that school cast from it is 15% stronger. Rewrite the page and the ink is spent again.
The Enochian orb is forged with one vial of hexed ink, of any school, in place of a second plain one.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hexed_vi: Hollow eyes, a shambling walk, weak swings at whoever comes near. Somebody's neighbour, under a witch's hex. You find them near covens, in abandoned churches, and near villages where a hedge witch has been at work.
You can kill one. Do that and its hex passes to you: jinxed and bad luck for two minutes, and nothing to show for it but rotten flesh.

Or free it. A salt round does it, and so does Break Hex: cast at it by name, or with it standing by the bowl. It slumps, straightens, and is a villager again, the very villager it was if a witch hexed one. It presses one to three emeralds on you and tells the village what you did.
A villager under a witch's hex
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.holy_oil: The one fire an angel fears. Pour it on the ground and it runs out in a ring two blocks wide and catches at once: an angel inside cannot leave until it burns out, and one who crosses the flames is burned.
Holy oil set alight is the one fire an angel cannot cross. Raphael's house has rings of it poured on the floor, dark and glossy: four of them, squares of oil round a patch of bare boards.

Set a ring alight while he stands inside it, with flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning arrow, and he is held there for six seconds: he cannot strike, cannot heal, and takes more from every blow. Then the ring burns out, and for a while no other ring will hold him.
He knows the oil and walks round it, but he does not think about it when he blinks or when he smites: lure him there. Lit or not, the rings are poured again at the start of every phase.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.holy_wat: Three bottles of water and a pinch of salt on a ritual altar, inside a small chalk ring, lit with flint and steel: three flasks of holy water. That is the first rite any hunter learns.
Throw it like a splash potion. It scalds demons. It scatters a ghost for a while. It shows a hellhound for what it is. In Hell, a dash of it eases the Torment.
You will pour more of it into rites and bowls than you ever throw. Make it by the dozen.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.horseman: Every time a Horseman falls his horse stays behind: red for War, black for Famine, sickly pale for Pestilence, pale as bone for Death. They have no powers, but they are better horses than any you could breed: tougher, faster, and they jump higher. Tame one, saddle it and ride.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.host_of_: Angels in their vessels, in suits, trench coats and fatigues, with breastplates, angel blades and tower shields: Michael's soldiers. They march in ranks and obey their captain, the one with the plumed helm and its wings open. While it stands they hold together; when it falls they break.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hosts_an: A General of the Host calls down a squad: a captain and four soldiers who follow you, fight what you fight and go back to Heaven after a minute.
A soldier of the Host, at a General's side
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hound_wh: Lilith keeps her dogs on a whistle, and she drops it when she dies. Blow it and a hellhound runs at your side for a minute, for a little mana.
Yours you can see. It goes for whatever hurts you and whatever you strike, and it never turns on a player. One at a time.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hungry_t: The First Blade. A great circle at night, lit with Ruby's knife: two bone blocks, three demon blood, a netherite ingot, a wither skeleton skull and a hellfire ember. It is bound to whoever forged it, and burns anyone else who holds it.

Feed it kills and it grows: at the third level it lets you lunge, and at the fifth, well fed, it will not let you die. Starve it and it feeds on you. It whispers. Do not listen. In the hand of one who bears the Mark of Cain it never hungers and strikes three times as hard.

The Whispering Codex is the same hunger in a book: a cursed catalyst, bound to its maker. Spells cast through it cost blood and sanity instead of mana, and they chain and pierce. Alone, it speaks the Forbidden Word, and whatever it marks takes more harm.
Watch your sanity with the Codex in hand. When it runs low, the words twist.
Famine's starving thralls. They pay you no mind: they shuffle to their master to be eaten, and every one that reaches him heals him. Kill them on the way.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hunter_r: A hunter who stays human can still rise: three ranks, each sworn at the altar. Only a human sworn to no side may take the oath, and choosing Heaven or Hell later gives the hunter's ranks up.

Hunter: the oath, sworn over a Colt bullet, four salt, two holy waters and a silver machete; your mana runs deeper (25 more for each rank). Veteran: a night's vigil over Lilith's and Metatron's trophies; supernatural things within 24 blocks glow faintly to you. Legend: the four Horsemen's rings and a Fallen Star; your hunter's weapons strike the supernatural a fifth harder, and possession slides off you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hunters_: Two strings, a gold ingot, and a drop of demon blood in the middle. It grows warm when something supernatural comes within sixteen blocks of you, and it steadies your hand: every kind of magic, sigil, bowl or rite, costs a tenth less mana while you wear it.
Wear it around your neck if you have the slot for it (Curios), or keep it in your hotbar or off hand.
Sneak and use your grimoire and the whole book opens. Four ribbons down the edge: Home, Journal, Scriptorium and Roadmap.

Home is the state of you: mana, sanity, what has changed you, any deal you owe on, and the next thing worth hunting. The Journal is these pages; mark the ones you need with a ribbon. The Scriptorium is where spells are composed, written into the grimoire or onto scrolls, and kept in a library for later.
The Roadmap is the long road from salt to the Cage, every hunt that matters laid out in order. What you have not found yet is a shadow on it.

A cap, a canvas jacket over flannel, jeans and work boots. Nothing an angel would look at twice, which is the point. Leather, iron and salt sewn into the seams, at any crafting table; about as tough as iron.
It ascends at the Hellforge like a weapon, up to IV. Each tier hardens it (at IV the whole set is as hard as armour gets) and gives it Aegis.

Aegis turns aside part of every blow a great enemy deals, even their Divine Wrath, the share of their blows that no armour, enchantment, potion or shield stops. A whole set gives 5% at I, 10% at II, 15% at III and 20% at IV; each piece a quarter of that. The General's armour is born at IV, and a fifth shard raises it to V: 30%, the hardest armour there is.

Your side adds to it. An angel gains 5% Aegis and two armour for each rank; a demon, two hearts for each rank; a hunter, a heart for each rank, and 5% Aegis against Divine Wrath. Aegis never turns aside more than 60%. Lesser creatures, and the enemies' own servants, are not great enough for it to matter.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hymnal_s: High on the mountains stand ruins of white stone, a stair winding up to a broken platform on the peak. To find one, draw a Hymnal Map: a small circle, a compass, a feather, a gold ingot, an amethyst shard and a holy water on the altar, and a blank map to light it.

Halfway up the stair stands a temple. Its window keeps the hymn, three panes read left to right, and its vault always keeps a Shattered Hymn. The rest of its chests hold holy water, salt, ink and, if you are lucky, a few of the Colt's rounds.
On the summit wait the Choir Altar and its seven bells. In a storm, the altar's light reaches the clouds. Read the Broken Chorus's page before you ring anything.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.kept_mem: Memories that belong together are worth more together. Gather a whole set and it stays with you, wherever you go.

Victories: five great enemies' falls make you a little harder to hurt by great enemies (+3% Aegis); every one of them, a heart more. The Crossroads: your deals' terms run a day longer. Cases: research runs a little faster at the desks. Kin: a deeper well of mana. Companions: your tamed pets close by heal over time. Sightings: ten first sightings, and you strike a little harder at every kind of creature you have seen (never the great enemies).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.key_to_t: The Key is forged, not found. A great circle, at night: a nether star, four hellfire embers, a gold block and two vials of Azazel's own blood. Nothing else will do for the blood. He has to fall first.

The Key lights the rite that opens the Cage, and later, the rifts that lead down into Hell. Lose to what is in the Cage and he leaves a cracked key behind him; a great circle at night, two embers and a demon blood make it whole again.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.knights_: Abaddon's own blade, left to whoever beats her the first time: a tier IV cursed cleaver. Use it and a wave of hellfire runs nine blocks down the ground before you, setting what it finds alight; then it needs six seconds. Without the Mark it hungers like the First Blade.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.last_sea: Sixty-six seals held the Cage shut, and Lilith was the last. When she dies, it breaks, and what is left of it falls at your feet.
Lucifer's summoning will not take without it, and the rite burns it. If he wins, the seal is gone with him: you will be calling Lilith up again before you get another try.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.0: The first demon. She only answers once Azazel is dead: a great circle at night, three demon blood, two hellfire embers, two bones and a vial of bound blood to sign her contract.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.1: Headstones rise in a ring around the circle. When she shines, the white light falls on everyone she can see: put a headstone between you. Each one takes two bursts before it falls, so keep moving. After each burst she is hollow for a moment, and that is when to hit her. In the end her light comes twice.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.2: If she writes your name, it is a contract. Everyone who can must wound her before it comes due, and holy wounds pay it down twice as fast. Burn it in time and she staggers. Fail, and hounds you cannot see come for whoever she named.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.linger_a: Two modifiers of the second tier from the bunker library. Each makes the spell cost half as much again.
Linger leaves a zone where the spell first takes hold: for four seconds it repeats the spell every second at half strength on whatever stands in it. One zone per cast.
Quicken lets your hand recover faster: the spell's wait, whichever of its sigils sets it, is cut by two fifths.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.locating: The smoke drifts toward what you seek and tells you which way, and roughly how far. What you put in the bowl decides what it looks for.
If what you seek is in another world, or nowhere at all, the smoke sinks back and the bowl keeps its contents.
To open the Cage: the great circle, at night, lit with the Key. Three demon blood, two hellfire embers, a holy water and the Last Seal on the altar.

Only holy things truly hurt him: angel blades, Smite, holy water. The Cage will not let you leave. Every attack is written on the ground first: red is fire, so move; blue is frost; violet is a beam, so break line of sight; gold is judgement. Hit hardest while he recovers after an attack.
He has four faces before the end: Lucifer, the Fallen, the Morningstar, and the Archangel Unbound, who takes to the air. If he wins, he walks back into the Cage and leaves a cracked key behind.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lucifer_: At the heart of Hell the Pit falls to the lava sea, and over it the Cage hangs on its chains. Under it, on the island, is the dais: draw the circle around its four stones, lay the four rings with two demon blood, a holy water and an ember, and open the Cage with the Key. He comes down in chains, and leaves them behind, one by one.

Six faces. The Prisoner. Hellfire. The cold of the Cage. Legion: kill the hounds, or they will drag you down. The Morning Star: watch for gold on the ground, the stars are falling. Light-Bringer: stand between the wings, and when he burns, find the green. Everything you learned against him still holds, but the floor will not.
If you fall, the rings stay on the stone. Beat him and the Cage is shut, and what he leaves behind is a fallen star, a load of rounds, two nether stars and a page of Smite.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lucifers: When Lucifer falls, a shard of his grace falls with him. Use it to take it in. Light pours into you, and it does not leave.
Your mana runs fifty deeper, for good. And the third-tier sigils, the pages written in the hand that burned your eyes, become legible. Echo among them.
You only get to carry one shard. The rest are no use to you; give them to someone who hunts with you.
A shard of an archangel's grace
Jump the shockwave when he lands. Break out of an ice cage with any tool. Hide behind ice from the grace beam. Reveal unmasks his illusions; strike one and it bursts.
The Snare only holds him while he recovers. When he gathers his grace, stand in a green sigil or inside a Ward, or die. Break his grace tether by running or by hitting him.
Beat him and he leaves everything: the Archangel Blade, his grace, the Colt and rounds for it, a nether star, the Echo sigil, and his likeness in stone.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.mana_and: Every sigil and every rite draws on your mana. You start with a hundred and it seeps back on its own, a couple of points a second. The blue bar shows where you stand.
It can run deeper. An archangel's grace adds fifty for good; the Darkness's mark adds twenty-five; a crossroads deal will sell you twenty-five more, at the usual price.

Sanity is the other bar, and most hunters never see it move. Some cursed things are paid for in your mind. Let it run low and you will hear whispers, and the words start to twist in your mouth. It comes back slowly on its own; a Purification steadies it at once.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.marks_of: What the witchcraft leaves on a body, as your own eyes will show it.

Agony: a pulse of harm every two seconds that stops at half a heart. Rot: now and then a bite of food in your pack turns to rotten flesh. Silenced: no sigil will come and no power answers. Marked: everything hurts a fifth more. Compelled: you follow, or you are drawn.
Name-Warded and Mirrored are the protections. Silver Edge counts down the silver blows you have left.
Each school trains on its own. A sigil teaches a fifth of the mana it cost; a bowl spell twice that for the same mana; a rite a third of its mana. Practice what you mean to be good at. Mastery stays with you through death.
An Apprentice (150) reads that school's second-tier pages, pays 5% less for its magic and has 5 more mana.
An Adept (600) reads third-tier pages, pays 10% less and has 10 more mana.
A Master (1800) reads a Master's pages, pays 15% less and has 20 more mana. Only your highest rank in any school adds mana: ranks in four schools do not add up to more.

Discounts add together and never take off more than 40%: being human saves 15% on all magic, the Hunter's Amulet 10%, and your rank in the spell's school the rest. A scroll still halves what is left on top of that.
A page beyond you stays unread, and you keep it. A page of no school, a form or a modifier, wants the rank in any school. What you have learned is never taken away.
Morningstar's Spark, what is left in you after you take in Lucifer's grace, reads every page as an Adept would. That is how Echo is read by those who never studied.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.memories: Heaven remembers your road even if you don't. The fall of every great enemy, every deal at the crossroads, every case closed or lost, every rank you rose to, the pets you buried, the first time you saw each creature and the one you hunted most: all of it is kept, even what happened before you ever came up here.

Twelve shrines line the lane, each holding one memory behind a shimmering veil. Step through a veil and the memory is staged before you, in the hollow at the end of the lane: the place as it was, the people as they stood. One of them glows. Touch it, and the memory is gathered: it gets its own page in the Memories tab of this book.

Walk out through the veil at the stage's edge, or stay away long enough, and the stage clears for the next. Only one memory plays at a time. The shrines show what you have not gathered first; once you have them all, others take their turn.
Gather three memories and the golden seal over the white wing opens. Somebody works in there.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.men_of_l: A brotherhood of scholars who watched the dark and wrote it all down, so that hunters could put it to rest. Angels, demons and plain hunters alike may join: the order cares what you know, not what you are.

Ranks are earned at the research desks. Aspirant on joining; Initiate after five pieces of research (the Men of Letters Ring: research runs a tenth faster); Scholar after fifteen, of three kinds (the Spellwright's Spectacles: worn, they show what hides); Master of Letters after thirty-five, of four kinds (Henry's Case: nine pockets for artifacts); Keeper of the Lore after seventy, of five kinds (the Aquarian Star: one more research at a time).
A member's book grows a tab no outsider ever sees: the Archive, where everything the order learns is kept.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.metatron: The Scribe of God. Once the Broken Chorus is silenced, write his name, Metatron, in a book and quill, and offer it in a great circle at night with two choir shards, a chrism, a holy water, two feathers and a glow ink sac.

He fights with a blade at first. Then his Hand writes burning words across the floor: get out of the strokes before they burn, jump the sweep, be elsewhere when the palm comes down. In the third act he takes to a lectern on a dais with two flights of stairs and will not leave it; climb, or strike from afar. His Book crushes, storms pages, and shuts on one of you until the others wound him enough.
At the last he takes up the Tablet and speaks the Word: BE STILL, LOOK AWAY or KNEEL. Obey it, to the letter, for the three seconds it holds. Watch the sky, too: angels fall burning where he points.
The eldest archangel, Heaven's general, and Lucifer's brother: the end of Heaven's road as Lucifer Uncaged is the end of Hell's. Once Metatron has fallen, call him down by day in a great circle in the Overworld with the Angel Tablet, the Seraph Wings, three choir shards and two holy waters, woken with an angel blade. Win or lose, the Tablet and the Wings fall back to earth.

He comes down into a Garden of Heaven wearing his vessel, a young man in a grey suit, and fights with an angel blade. When his palm starts to shine, never let it reach your brow: break his reach or turn it with a shield. He will ask you for your yes. Say it, and for a while he wears you: your body walks to your friends and burns them, and he heals; when he lets go, his grace stays with you and your blows land twice as hard on him. Say no, or say nothing, and the Host of Heaven hunts you.

Then the Host of Heaven takes the field, in ranks behind its captain; strike the captain down and they break. In the War in Heaven his shadow spreads its wings: his lance pins whoever it strikes and stays in the ground until he calls it back (he is quicker without it, but his reach is short). Then he takes to the sky with storms of steel feathers and dives; when he lands to gather himself, strike.

In the Throne Room his vessel burns away and his true form stands up: a general in white and gold, four blocks and more, six wings of steel and a halo of spears. When the halo breaks, his lance can be pulled from the ground and thrown back at him.
What he leaves, for every hunter, every time
And one piece of his armour you do not have yet
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.michaels: Lucifer's brother's grace. Take it in, once, and it stays with you. Wear the Seraph Wings on your back (or in your chest slot) and they will carry you as freely as a bird, for as long as their strength lasts; run them dry in the air and they fold, and you drift down. Touch the ground to let them rest.
The one weapon an archangel fears from another. Throw it and it comes back to your hand; it strikes angels and demons twice as hard and pins what it strikes for a moment.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.name_war: Protection is laid on you, or on whoever a taglock in the bowl names. It needs no blood.
Under a Ward of the Name every curse and binding aimed at you fails, and stings whoever spoke it; scrying shows them nothing; Hex and the curse bags slide off you.
A Mirror Hex sends the next curse back to its caster and breaks. A caster under their own Ward shrugs off what comes back.
Ward of the Name: ten minutes
Mirror Hex: twenty minutes, or until it breaks
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.0: When an angel starts asking questions, Heaven sends it to Naomi. She sits it in a chair, puts a drill to its eye and keeps going until the questions stop; then she sends it back to work. A calm, severe woman in a grey suit and a white coat, she has run that room for longer than humans have had words.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.1: Her room is the white wing of your own Heaven. Its seal opens once you have gathered three memories; walk in and she is waiting, with the chairs, the console and the guards. There is no rite. Nobody else's road needs her: she is a challenge, not a duty.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.2: I. Intake. Her open palm comes down in a gold circle (raise a shield as it lands and she staggers); a gold ring holds whoever stands in it. A line runs from a chair to whoever stands most alone: if it catches you, you are strapped in (The Chair, in this book). She lunges with the drill in a cone and leaves you bleeding. A white ring spreads from her to wipe your mind: step into its green gaps, or see nothing for a while and move slowly after.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.3: She calls her guards, and while two of them stand she takes less from every blow. She stages a training test with copies of the people you love (The Training Test, in this book). When she is hurt she walks to the console and heals herself until somebody strikes it six times.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.4: II. Reprogramming. At half her strength the room changes round you and she stops being patient: the drill lunges three times in a row, and the chair holds harder.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.5: An angel of the second rank or more is the first one she straps in: you are one of hers, and you should sit. A demon feels the drill more.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.6: Once she has fallen, the room stays quiet when you walk in. Crouch as you cross into it to call her back.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.7: Met again, she leaves her bust, and now and then her drill or her diadem. Like every great enemy, she also leaves a shard for the Hellforge and, the first time, a heart of Vitality. And the lift at the back of her room starts working.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.ca: What she leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomis_d: A thin band of white gold she wore to keep her own head clear. Carry it in your other hand, or as a charm: nothing can condition you, mark you for Heaven or possess you, and great enemies hurt you a little less (+3% Aegis).

The drill she used on angels for a thousand years: a holy weapon of the fourth tier. Strike the same creature three times and its will is yours: for ten seconds it fights for you. It never works on a great enemy. Raise it at the Hellforge and it holds them longer.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.on_angel: Forget the halos. An angel is a soldier, old as the world and twice as proud, and most of what hurts a demon does nothing to one. Salt, traps and exorcism: no.
Holy things are what works. Angel blades, the Smite sigil, holy water, a Sanctity rune graven in your weapon. Watch the ground, too: everything an archangel does is written on it first.
The ones in this book: Lucifer in his Cage, the Broken Chorus over the mountains, and Metatron, who writes everything down.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.penumbra: Penumbra, the blade that drinks the light, left by the Darkness. It drinks light from bright places and from lit foes. Hold use and let go for an Umbra Wave that blinds and wounds, stronger the more light it holds. It cuts deeper in the dark.

The Eclipse Sight is a vial of her own sight. Drink it and you are marked for good: darkness and blindness cannot take you, the eclipse cannot hide the world, hellhounds are plain to see, and your mana runs twenty-five deeper.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.pestilen: Sickly, coughing, with glasses and a cane, and sorry for nothing. Call him with a fermented spider eye, mushrooms and clotted blood, once Lucifer has fallen. His ground is a toxic swamp.

Toxic clouds grow over the swamp and everything he does gives you the plague. Then the flies come: swarms that chase and blind and only burn. On his sickly horse he leaves a trail of plague and coughs cones of it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.pet_coll: Leather, string and an iron nugget. Use the collar on a tamed animal of yours and it wears the twin of it; the one in your hand is the link.
With the collar in the bowl you can find a lost pet, and the collar comes back to you. If the worst has happened, there is a spell for that too.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.0: Pestilence's plague stacks up to five times. Every stack eats a little more of you, takes a heart off your health while it lasts and stops you healing on your own. It does not wear off by itself while he keeps giving it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.1: While he fights, antidote vials turn up in dry spots of his swamp. Drink one: the plague is gone and none takes for fifteen seconds.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.2: His flies only burn: hit them with a Fire Aspect blade or a burning arrow, light them with flint and steel, lead them through fire, or walk into them burning.
Raphael, the archangel who heals and the archangel who smites. With the Horsemen loose and Lucifer free, he means to finish the Apocalypse his brothers started. He wears a tall, stern man in a dark suit and a long black coat, and he only comes down in a thunderstorm.

Wait for thunder, then lay two holy oils, a lightning rod, a glistering melon, a golden apple and two feathers in a grace circle in the Overworld, after War, Famine and Pestilence are beaten, and wake it with an angel blade (it is not used up). He comes down in a bolt where the altar stood, and an old abandoned house stands round you. The storm will not lift until it is over. Nobody else's road needs him: he is a challenge, not a duty.

I. The Storm. Inside the house he calls lightning on you (a violet mark on the floor first: move), claps thunder that throws you back, blinks from place to place with a flinch of wings, and sends bolts through the broken windows in lines. When he raises his hand and it burns, he is about to smite: hit him hard enough, or catch the blow on a raised shield, and the smite breaks.

II. The Healer. He calls his garrison, and each angel holds a thread of grace to him that heals him while it lasts. Stand in a thread to cut it, or cut the angel down; once, he lays his hands on a fallen one and raises it. (His Garrison, in this book.)

III. Wrath of Heaven. He tears the roof off the house. Lightning falls in fields and leaps from one of you to the next, every flash throws the shadow of his wings across the walls, and his veins burn with light. When he snaps his fingers the air bursts all round him: only a green band halfway out is safe.
All through the fight there are rings of holy oil on the floor. Light one with him inside it and the storm is yours for a moment. (The Holy Oil Trap, in this book.)
Called again, he leaves his trophy, and now and then his staff. Like every great enemy, he also leaves a shard for the Hellforge and, the first time, a heart of Vitality.
What he leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.raphaels: A tall staff of black wood bound in silver, crowned with a cage that holds a crystal of the storm. It is a holy catalyst of the fourth tier: your sigils cast through it.

Its own spell is lightning that leaps from foe to foe, up to three of them near you. Sneak as you use it and it lays a healing grace on you and your allies close by instead; that needs a while before it answers again. Both grow with its Ascension at the Hellforge.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.0: In Death's fight every hunter carries a clock of about a minute, a pocket watch in the corner of the eye. Hitting Death or killing a reaper winds it back to full. A reaper's touch takes time off it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.1: Reapers are only seen by those whose time is nearly up (under twenty seconds), by those in limbo, and by everyone once the world of the dead holds the arena.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.2: When a clock runs out its hunter falls into limbo: the world goes grey and only the reapers and a light remain. Reach the light within fifteen seconds and you walk back out. Otherwise, you die.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reprogra: A white leather chair with straps at the wrists and ankles, and over it, on a jointed arm, the drill. When her line catches you, you are in it, and you cannot get up.

Struggle: press jump as fast as you can. Eighteen good pulls in four seconds break the straps; in her second phase it takes twenty-four in three and a half. A human's will makes it easier; an angel was made to sit still, and it is harder. A friend can free you with three blows to the chair.

Fail, and the drill comes down: a twentieth of your strength and more, through any armour, and for a few seconds you are Conditioned (your blows against angels fall soft). She heals a little, and lets you go.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.research: Sit at a research desk and the order's board offers you topics: formulas (new sigils for the grimoire), rites (new bowl spells), the identity of a cursed artifact, a creature's file, a great enemy's file, the write-up of a solved case, and the Archive's own lore. Higher tiers open with higher ranks.

Each costs field notes of its kind, paper and ink. Field notes come from the creatures you kill as a member, from chests in the world's ruins and from solved cases. Research runs on game time, even while you are away; when it is done, its page is in the Archive.

You never carry field notes: they go straight into your Archive, and the desk takes them from there. The Archive's Field Notes shelf counts what you have, and each creature's file says how many you hold on it. Loose notes someone else left lying about are filed the moment you pick them up or use them.
A creature's file has no end: every level adds to your damage against that kind of creature (never against the great enemies), less with each level.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rites_of: The angel's ranks, from the first Grace to the Host. Each needs the rank before it.
The demon's ranks after the crossroads. Each needs the rank before it.
The hunter's oaths, and the rites that undo a side and bless the ground.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ritual_c: The small circle: eight chalk lines around the altar, nothing else. The binding circle: a 5x5 chalk square with a lit candle on each corner. The blood circle is the same square drawn in blood chalk.

The great circle is the one for summonings: a ring of blood chalk nine wide, with six lit black candles inside it. The void circle is a ring of the same size broken by crying obsidian at its four points, with four black candles close around the altar.
There is one more circle, drawn only around four old stones under the Cage in Hell. If you ever need it, you will know.
Blood chalk: four chalk and a demon's blood
Chalk, blood chalk, black candle, crying obsidian
Every rite starts with an altar: polished blackstone bricks, a gold ingot and a candle. Set it down, and draw the circle the rite asks for around it, on the same level, with chalk lines and candles lit where it wants them.

Lay the offerings on the altar one at a time, then light the rite with what it asks for, flint and steel more often than not. Some rites want the night, some the day, some a certain place. The rite takes its mana up front.

If the circle is wrong, red sparks mark the first bad block. Once it is burning, never smudge a line or snuff a candle: the circle breaks, lightning falls, it burns you, and something comes through that should not.

A rite that cannot be answered spends nothing: if another fight already holds the world, the summoning is refused before it starts and the altar says where that fight is; if nothing answers in the end, what lit it comes back to you.

The keys of the road (the Last Seal, the Key to the Cage, the Shattered Hymn, the Rings, the Fallen Star and their like) are never lost. Lose the fight, flee it, or have the world stop in the middle of it, and they come back to whoever offered them, straight into their pack or as soon as they return. They do not burn and never vanish from the ground, and every hunter who fought a great enemy takes their own.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rival_hu: Other hunters work these roads too: in a leather jacket, a flannel shirt or a long coat, with a sawn-off shotgun loaded with rock salt, a machete and a flask of holy water. To a human they are friends, and they will help you against demons. To an angel or a demon they are death: they come by night, shoot from range, close in with the machete and throw holy water at whatever has black eyes.
What they carry: salt, holy water, and once in a while a bullet for the Colt.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.0: Three hundred years a witch, thrown out of the Grand Coven for being better than them, and not shy about it. She will not fight you in her own house. Talk to her.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.1: She teaches for a price, copying Witchcraft pages out for you herself: five at most on offer, the lowest tier first, only pages you do not know and your Witchcraft mastery lets you learn. A first-tier page costs eight emeralds; a second-tier one sixteen, two gold ingots and two amethyst shards; a third-tier one twenty-four, four gold and a ghast tear. A Master's page she keeps for her allies, and only one: see Unmark.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.2: Every page you buy earns a little of her trust, and some pages she keeps for those she trusts: her own Familiar Bond only after five. She also sells three taglocks for three emeralds, and Witchcraft hexed ink for six.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.3: She hears things. Ask her the right question at the right time, and she may tell you where to find someone you would rather not meet.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena_a: When the Grand Witch's last phase begins, Rowena comes out of her own smoke beside you. Nothing touches her. She keeps near the hunters, throws a bolt at the coven every five seconds, and when the Grand Witch takes everyone's lock of hair she draws the green circles to stand in.
When it is over she watches the Grand Witch fall, and goes home. That is where she will take the Mark off you.
Rowena, on your side for once
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena_b: Only for the one who kept the Book. Read it in her house at night, within the twelve-block ring round the middle of her house (or a few blocks past it), and she steps out of yellow smoke. Her house is the arena, and it is put back as it was afterwards. Three phases, a third of her strength each.
The Witch at Home: a flick of the wrist down a violet lane that throws whoever is in it; Ignis, a red circle where you stand and then fire; Glacies, a blue one, and frost that slows you to a crawl.

The Familiar and the Hexed: a raven answers her and goes for a lock of your hair. While it holds one, every six seconds she sends a curse down it, pain or frailty, wherever you hide. Kill the raven and the lock drops; she calls another twenty seconds later. Her hexed victims shamble at you: kill one and she heals four parts in a hundred; free it with Break Hex or a salt round and it costs her three. Yellow smoke where she is about to appear: step out of it.

The Recitation: she rises into the air and recites over three bowls for fifteen seconds. Smash them: three blows each. Break all three and she drops, stunned for five seconds and taking half as much again. Leave any whole and for the last three seconds the whole house glows red; then the hex sweeps it, twelve for every bowl still standing.
When she falls the Grand Witch walks out of the smoke for whoever kept the Book. Read it again while sneaking, in her house at night, for a rematch.
What she leaves: her Grimoire and her bust the first time (a bust in a rematch)
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowenas_: "R. MacLeod. Spells, Hexes, Discretion." An embossed card in green ink, taken off a coven witch. The ink is not quite dry, and it never will be: it runs toward its owner's door.
Use it in the Overworld and it tells you which way the ink runs and roughly how far. Anywhere else the ink only pools. No ordinary map leads to her house.

With Lucifer back in his box, Rowena told me where Cain is. The Father of Murder, the first demon-killer and the first Knight of Hell, keeps bees now: a little farm out where the roads give up, honey and silence.

Her own book, left to whoever beats her the first time: a tier IV catalyst. It remembers the last aimed spell you spoke at a spell bowl while you carried it (a curse, a binding, a banishing: anything that needs a target, never a brew) and what named its target.

Use it and it speaks that spell again, at once, with no bowl and no recitation, for the spell's usual mana, at most once a minute. Nothing from the remembered bowl is spent. Hold a taglock or a vial of bound blood in your other hand and it aims at them instead. If the spell finds nothing to act on, it does not count.

Somewhere between twelve hundred and thirty-two hundred blocks from the middle of the world, where a forest meets open ground, stands a house far nicer than it has any right to be: a garden, a library, a workroom with a spell bowl. Every world has exactly one.
Its owner is home whenever a hunter is about. She would like you to wipe your boots.
A House at the Forest's Edge
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rubys_kn: An iron sword, two demon blood and a hellfire ember on the altar of a blood circle. It cuts demons deeper than steel should.
A demon slain with it always bleeds: the blood is yours every time, smoke or no smoke. Cold iron, too, so it scatters a ghost. Later it is the key to something worse.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.0: A blank rune is smooth stone, chalk and Enochian ink. Carve it at a small circle: the offerings on the altar, the blank in your hand to light it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.1: For blades: Edge cuts deeper (a tenth of the blade's damage, at least a point and a half), Ember sets alight, Frost slows, Leech heals you from what you deal, Swiftness quickens your swing. For catalysts: Resonance makes spells cheaper and harder, Focus brings them back faster, Echo makes them repeat now and then. Sanctity fits anything and makes every blow holy.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.2: Two runes come only from the great ones. Void, from what the Darkness leaves, carved at night: it drinks the light, and only a tier IV weapon will take it. Hymn, from the Chorus's shards: every fourth blow or spell rings out again as holy light.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.0: Salt is your first friend. Rock salt shows up in the stone like any ore, deeper as deepslate. No ore nearby? Boil a bucket of water dry in a furnace.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.1: Pour it on the ground as a line. You can walk over it; a demon cannot. It is a wall to them, solid as stone, and they will walk the long way round rather than test it. A ghost cannot cross it either.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.2: Salt will not stop the great ones. Nothing you pour on the floor holds a boss. Keep a stack on you anyway: the exorcism, the binding, the bones of a restless grave and half the bowl spells want it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.cap: Rock salt, in stone and deepslate
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt_and: A lonely graveyard, one to three graves on flat dry ground, headstones and mounds of grave soil. Only one of them is restless. Its bones lie two blocks under the end of the mound by the headstone.

Dig the soil and the dirt under it until the bones are bare; while the spirit is restless, they will not break. Salt them. Then set them alight with flint and steel or a fire charge. The ghost goes with them, for good. A Banishing does the same from the bowl.
One grave in each yard hides a chest under the foot of its mound. Grave dirt from the mounds goes into hex bags and darker work.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.seraph_w: Six wings, what is left of the Broken Chorus when it is silenced. Worn on the back (Curios), they rest, fold when you crouch, and open wide when you fall.
They will not carry you anywhere. They are only for show, and what a show.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.shapeshi: It wears somebody else: a villager at the edge of town, or, on a case, the face of a hunter you know. In its borrowed skin it shrugs off most of what you do to it.
Weakness: silver, or a true sight (Second Sight, or the Spellwright's Spectacles), shows it for what it is. Found out, its skin sloughs off and it takes every blow in full.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_ef: The effects are what the spell does. You cannot draw the same one twice in a spell.

Smite is holy force, twice as hard on demons and the dead. Hellfire burns flesh and a pinch of sulfur. Frost slows, freezes, and turns still water to ice. Mend closes wounds and smothers flames. Repel throws the target away from you. Reveal strips invisibility, outlines what it touches and unmasks illusions.

Two are a hunter's sigils. Exorcise is agony to a demon, and casts a trapped one out entirely; it burns salt. The Snare (once called Bind) holds a demon for a breath, two seconds, as a devil's trap would, and roots anything else to the spot for as long. It is a moment's grace, not a cage: paint a trap for the real holding.

A spell written with the old Bind still works: every page, scroll and formula that names it casts the Snare. Each effect belongs to one of the four schools, and the first effect decides the spell's (see The Four Schools).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_fo: A spell is a form, up to three effects and up to three modifiers. The form is how it reaches the world.

Touch takes whatever is within arm's reach; a helpful spell with nothing there falls back on you. Bolt is thrown and flies straight until it hits something. Burst is a pulse outward from you. Ward is a circle at your feet that keeps working and stops hostile projectiles.
Touch and Bolt are cheap and quick. Burst and Ward cost more and your hand needs longer to recover. Ward is the harder sigil to come by, and the one you will want when something big starts to glow.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_mo: Modifiers bend a spell and multiply its cost. Empower makes the effects stronger. Extend makes them last longer and reach further. Widen spreads them over an area.
Echo makes the spell repeat itself a moment later. It is written in a hand no one can follow until they are an Adept in some school, or carry Morningstar's Spark. Lucifer carries a page of it.
The Scriptorium shows the cost of a spell as you build it. Watch it: three modifiers on a Burst will empty you in one cast.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_pa: Demons carry scraps of their masters' grimoires. Kill one and now and then a torn sigil page falls out of it; occultists carry them far more often than the black-eyed brawlers. Read a page to learn its sigil for good.

The harder pages are written in a hand that burns your eyes. A second-tier page wants an Apprentice of its school, a third-tier one an Adept, a Master's page a Master; a page of no school (a form, a modifier) wants that rank in any school. Keep the ones you cannot read yet: see Mastery. Morningstar's Spark reads them like an Adept.
The Scriptorium keeps an encyclopedia of every sigil: the ones you know, and the shapes of the ones you do not.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigils_o: Three Enochian effects are found where the choir once sang: Radiance and Halo in the temples of the Hymnal Spires, and in their vaults, one time in three, Judgement.
Radiance (second tier) is a blinding flash: a little harm, two and a half times that on the unholy, three seconds of blindness and five of a glowing outline. A boss only takes the burn.
Halo (second tier) is helpful: a ring of golden hearts that soaks up harm for fifteen seconds. It never touches a foe.

Judgement is a Master's sigil and costs a holy water. It marks the ground under its target; a moment and a half later a column of light falls there and every foe within two and a half blocks takes 16 harm, half as much again if unholy. Whatever moved away in time is spared.
Radiance
Halo
Judgement
Sigils of Heaven
Crowley's Corridors keep the Infernal pages: their chests hold Brimstone, Hellchain and, more rarely, Soul Rend.
Brimstone (second tier) burns a pinch of sulfur and leaves a cloud of burning sulphur where it lands: five pulses of hellfire a second apart, on every foe within two blocks of that spot.
Hellchain (second tier) is a chain of hellfire that burns the target and drags it to you. A boss is too heavy to drag: it only burns.
Soul Rend (third tier) tears at the soul for 5 harm, and you drink half of what it actually does.
Brimstone
Hellchain
Soul Rend
Sigils of Hell
Witchcraft written as sigils. Old graves give up Hex and Pain; Glamour is shelved in the bunker library.
Hex (first tier) lays a jinx for fifteen seconds. Bosses shrug it off, and a protection bag or a Ward of the Name turns it away.
Pain (second tier) is harm that goes straight through armour, and a limp: Slowness for three seconds. A boss takes the harm and no more.

Glamour (third tier) is helpful: you, or a friend, turn unseen for five seconds, and every creature hunting you within sixteen blocks sees an enemy in the nearest other creature instead, or loses the scent. Bosses are never fooled.
Hex
Pain
Glamour
Sigils of the Craft
Plain hunter's work. Salt Shot turns up in graves; Silver Edge in the bunker library.
Salt Shot (first tier) burns a salt: a blast of rock salt that scatters a ghost, breaks a possession and hits a demon two and a half times as hard, knocking it back. Anything else is only stung.

Silver Edge (second tier) lays three charges on your hands for a minute: the next three blows of whatever you hold, even a bare fist, count as silver against werewolves and shapeshifters. Each blow that lands spends one.
Salt Shot
Silver Edge
Sigils of the Hunt
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.silver_m: Three iron ingots, a salt and a holy water in a small circle. Cheap, and made for one thing.
Strikes from behind are double criticals, and a kill from behind takes the head. Get behind them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_bo: Older than sigils and slower: witchcraft, the way Bobby did it. Five copper ingots and a gold one make the bowl. Set it on solid ground.

Pour in up to four bottles and drop in up to eight ingredients, nothing spare: the mix has to be exactly what the spell asks for. Light it with flint and steel or a fire charge, then speak the Latin before the fire dies. Typing errors cost time; accents and spaces do not matter.
A mix no spell answers to blows up in your face: black smoke, a burn, something nasty for a while, and everything in the bowl is lost. Words you never learned do nothing at all.
Sneak with empty hands to lift the bowl, contents and all. It takes both hands, and it spills if you jump, fall or get hit. Put in your pack, it keeps everything.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_pa: You cannot cast what you do not know the words to. Loose pages with a spell written out, Latin and all, turn up in old graves and forgotten chests, and demons carry them: occultists more often than the black-eyed kind.
A master librarian will sell you one for emeralds and a book. And a crossroads demon who comes back angry always has one on it.
Read a page to learn its spell, with every recipe for it; the page is used up. Once you know a spell, this journal keeps its recipes for you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_sc: Any spell you can compose you can write out in full on a scroll: a sheet of paper and a vial of Enochian ink each. The Scriptorium writes them in batches if you have the paper and ink for it.
A scroll is read aloud once and burns up. Anyone can read one, sigils known or not, and it costs half the mana the spell would. Hand them to whoever hunts with you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.taglocks: A twist of paper and string. Use a blank taglock on a creature or a player to snip a lock of their hair; sneak and use it in the air to take your own.
Snipping is quiet but not invisible: one time in four they notice. A beast turns on you; a person is told someone tugged at their hair, and by whom.

In the bowl a filled taglock names whom the spell is for, as a dose of someone's blood does, and no recipe counts it as an ingredient: drop it in beside the rest. If someone's blood is poured in as well, the blood speaks first.
Locating a person: water, and their blood poured in or their taglock
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_arse: Every blade and catalyst worth carrying is forged by ritual, not at a crafting table, and each has a tier, from I to IV, and room for one to three runes. The tier sets what graving them costs.
Catalysts are held opposite a grimoire, in the other hand, and change your spells; alone, they have a spell of their own. The heavier weapons are swung by charging: hold use, then let go.
Holy weapons count as holy wherever they land. That matters more than their edge against the things at the end of this book.
None of them, as forged, is enough for the great enemies. Each can be ascended at the Hellforge with the shards those enemies leave, tier by tier, up to V (see Ascension).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_bunk: Out in open country, three to five thousand blocks from the world's heart, a little stone hut sits on a hillside that nobody looks at twice. Behind its steel door, iron stairs go down into the Men of Letters' bunker. Henry's map marks it; no compass will.

Only the Bunker Key opens the vault door. Below: the war room with its war table, the library with its research desks and archive shelves, a lab, a dungeon with a devil's trap painted on the floor, an armoury, a garage and the dormitories. Its desks, its door and its table yield only to members.
The war room and the library
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_cage: At the heart of Hell, at its very centre, the Pit falls sheer to the lava sea. Over it, on its chains, hangs the Cage, and under the Cage an island with a dais and four old stones.
Lucifer waits inside, in chains, head bowed. Now and then he looks up at whoever has come so far. Nothing can touch him while the Cage is shut.
The iris in its floor opens only for the four rings and the Key. When it does, he comes down.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_choi: Abaddon is dead and her Book is in my pack. Somewhere in it is the cure for the Mark of Cain, and only a witch can read it. I know exactly one witch who would not kill me on sight.

Take it to Rowena and speak of it. She will ask for it. Give it to her and she is in your debt, and against her old sisters of the Grand Coven she will stand with you. Keep it and she will not forgive you: she will want it back, and she will take it if she can.
Either way it is final. You choose once, for good, and a second copy of the Book changes nothing.
What to Do with the Book
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_colt: A Paterson revolver, 1836, five chambers. Samuel Colt made it for one job. There's nothing this gun can't kill. Lucifer carries it, loaded, and leaves it when he falls.

One round kills any living thing outright: any demon, monster, shade, echo or illusion, any beast. Not a hunter (unless the server allows it), and not archangels or anything above them. Against a great enemy it strikes a twentieth of its full strength that no armour blunts (the Author, far less), though it will not carry them past one of their turning points. Use to fire; sneak-use or the reload key seats one round at a time.
The rounds cannot be crafted. Once you have held the Colt, forge them by night in a blood circle, eight at a time. A few lie in the Hymnal Spire's temple, and with the great ones when they fall.
Some hunters write their own rules. The Endless Colt is the same gun, always loaded: it never spends a round and never needs reloading. No rite or grave gives it; it is only found in creative mode.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_deal: What it offers, and what it costs in days before the hounds come. Two more hearts, or twenty-five more mana, yours for good: five days. Everything you dropped at your last death that nobody picked up, or a dead pet back on its feet: seven days.

Something rare from its pockets, bullets, embers, shards and the like: ten days. Knowledge: a map to what hides nearby, a Hymnal Spire or a restless grave, or failing that, a book on how to kill the next great thing you have not killed yet: ten days.
The contract tells you whose soul, for what, and how long you have. Keep it. You will need it if you mean to break the deal.
The contract it leaves in your hands
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_debt: On the last day you will hear the dogs. When it falls due, a pack of three to five hellhounds comes for you, wherever you are. Survive the hunt, by killing the pack or lasting two minutes, and the debt is paid.
Die while they are on you and the debt is paid another way. You come back, but not all of you: for three days you are two hearts short and your mana does not return.

Or break it. Burn the contract in a bowl, with holy water, salt and a hellfire ember, and the demon who holds it walks again, angry. Kill it before your time runs out and the contract is void. If it flees its vessel, it comes back another night.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_dock: Everything in Heaven was written before it happened, and from his third phase Zachariah stops pretending otherwise.
